# Pipeup: the specification in brief

**Status:** 9 designed journeys · last updated 2026-11-10 · **Open questions:** [2](../open-questions.md)

Pipe up, right where the work is.

## The problem
People share work as standalone HTML files: reports, specs, prototypes and slide decks, many of them written by AI agents. Those files have no good way to collect feedback. Reviewers reply in chat threads that lose the context of what they were looking at, and the author (or the agent working for them) has to guess where each remark belongs.

## What it gives them
Pipeup turns any HTML page into a reviewable document with one script tag. Reviewers select words, click a block or drop a pin and comment in place. Comments stay in their own browser, and Copy comments as Markdown turns them into text that says exactly where each comment is, ready to send to the author or paste into an AI agent.

## Who it is for
- **Maya Lindqvist**, Reviewer; reads a colleague's HTML report or deck and says what she thinks: someone sent them an HTML file; they want to say what they think about a sentence, a block or a spot, and hand it back, with no account to make. Goal: Say what she thinks about a sentence, a block or a spot on the page, and hand it back without making an account.
- **Tom Adeyemi**, Author; writes reports and decks as HTML, often with a coding agent, and asks people to review them: they made the page (or an agent did), add one line to it, and want every comment pinned to the exact place so an agent can act on it. Goal: Collect every reviewer's comments pinned to the exact place, and hand them to an agent that acts on them.

## Decisions needed

2 questions are open. [All of them, with where each is asked](../open-questions.md).

- How will this be observed: moderated sessions, or something counted?
- How many pastes, and who judges that the agent found the place?

## Success criteria
- **SC-001** A reviewer with no account comments on a sentence within a minute of opening the page. Measure: **Open question:** How will this be observed: moderated sessions, or something counted?
- **SC-002** An author pastes copied comments into a coding agent and the agent finds every place without asking. Measure: **Open question:** How many pastes, and who judges that the agent found the place?

## Out of scope
- Reviewing images or PDFs on their own.
- A hosted service, accounts, dashboards or notifications: sharing and live review are optional add-ons the author chooses.
- Rich comments: formatting, images or embedded content. Comments are plain text with line breaks and links.
- Replacing the chat or tracker where decisions are made; Pipeup collects the feedback and hands it on.
